content: There are approximately 5 million elderly and disabled individuals across the nation. The National Center for Assisted Living (NCAL) operates as a division of the American Health Care Association (AHCA). AHCA/NCAL collaborates with the United States Congress and the federal government to advocate for long-term care services. Membership in the organization is available to both small and large healthcare facilities, as well as to professionals such as long-term care administrators, directors of nursing, certified nursing assistants, and facility owners and operators. The AHCA distributes a weekly email newsletter called Capitol Connection and a monthly magazine titled Provider. These publications deliver breaking news and updates on legislative developments, regulations, and issues impacting the long-term care industry. Additionally, the association provides opportunities for professional development, education, and networking. In 2007, AHCA/NCAL launched the Advancing Excellence in America’s Nursing Homes campaign, which aims to enhance the quality of care provided in nursing homes. Furthermore, the AHCA established National Nursing Home Week in 1967. This is a week-long observance dedicated to recognizing nursing homes, held annually in May. It begins on Mother’s Day, which is the second Sunday of May in the United States.
